title: A permissible blowup preserves the boundary and its strict exceptional part
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian regular scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme], Noetherian meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact (every open cover has a finite subcover), let $B\subset X$ be a normal crossings divisor, and let $H\subset B$ be a reduced union of irreducible components which is a strict normal crossings divisor; $H=\varnothing$ is allowed. A normal crossings divisor means a reduced effective Cartier divisor (its ideal is locally generated by one non-zero-divisor) [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal] which, etale locally [def-weil-etale-morphism], has equation $t_1\cdots t_r=0$ for distinct members of a regular system of parameters; a regular system of parameters in a regular local ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$ is a set of $\dim R$ elements generating $\mathfrak m$. Here a strict normal crossings divisor has regular irreducible components, and every intersection of $s$ distinct components is empty or regular with every irreducible component of codimension $s$ in $X$. Let $M\subset B$ be a regular closed subscheme such that etale locally at each point of $M$, in parameters giving the above equation for $B$, its ideal is generated by a nonempty subset of those parameters. Let $b:X^+=\operatorname{Bl}_M(X)\to X$ [def-nagata-global-blowup], let $E=(b^{-1}M)_{\mathrm{red}}$, and put $B^+=(b^{-1}B)_{\mathrm{red}}$ and $H^+=(b^{-1}(H\cup M))_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then $X^+$ is regular, $B^+$ is a normal crossings divisor, and $H^+$ is a strict normal crossings divisor and a union of irreducible components of $B^+$. In particular $H^+$ has finitely many regular irreducible components and every intersection of $s$ distinct components is empty or regular of codimension $s$ in $X^+$. As reduced closed subschemes, $B^+=B^{\mathrm{st}}\cup E$ and $H^+=H^{\mathrm{st}}\cup E$, where the superscript denotes strict transform [def-nagata-strict-transform].

source.place: Expose VIII 4.1.2--4.1.4(i), printed p. 117; Lemma 4.2.9 and its coordinate-chart proof, printed p. 121; the regular-intersection criterion is Remark 4.2.2(i), printed p. 118.
